2. The complainant had obtained a Shopkeepers Insurance Policy from the
respondent Insurance Company for coverage of his business stock and allied
risks, for the period 22.06.2007 to 21.06.2008. During the subsistence of the said
policy, a fire incident occurred on 06.12.2007, resulting in substantial loss and
damage to the insured goods and property of the complainant. The said incident
admittedly fell within the currency of the insurance policy, and thus, the
complainant lodged a claim with the Insurance Company seeking indemnification
of the loss suffered due to the fire. Upon intimation of the loss, the Insurance
Company appointed a licensed surveyor, namely Mr. Sunil Kumar P. Bhatt, to

assess and verify the extent of damage and the genuineness of the claim. The
complainant, as averred, duly cooperated in the survey proceedings and
submitted the requisite documents, including purchase invoices, stock details,
and other financial records in support of the claim. After conducting the survey
and examining the materials placed on record, the surveyor submitted his
detailed report on 27.08.2008. However, within a short span of 48 hours, i.e., on
29.08.2008, the Insurance Company repudiated the claim of the complainant.
The same is reproduced herein below for ready reference:

2.1 The repudiation as seen, was primarily based on the alleged violation of
Condition No. 6-B of the policy, on the ground that the complainant had failed to
Page 2 of 29
furnish proper proof and relevant information with respect to the claim. It was
further alleged by the Insurance Company that, during the course of the survey,
certain invoices submitted by the complainant were found to be fraudulent,
manipulated, or altered, and therefore, the claim was not admissible. The
complainant has denied these allegations and asserted that all documents
submitted, including invoices and payment records, were genuine and duly
supported by corresponding financial transactions, including bank account
entries. It has been the specific case of the complainant that the repudiation was
carried out in a mechanical and arbitrary manner, without proper appreciation of
the material on record, and that the Insurance Company failed to conduct a fair
and reasonable assessment of the claim. Aggrieved by the wrongful repudiation
of his legitimate claim, the complainant filed a consumer complaint before the
State Commission alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice on the
part of the Insurance Company. The complainant contended that the loss
suffered due to the fire was duly covered under the policy, that all necessary
documents were furnished, and that the repudiation of the claim on vague and
unsubstantiated grounds was illegal and unjustified. The complainant, therefore,
had prayed that the Insurance Company to pay a sum of Rs.37,16,627/- along
with interest @ 12% per annum from the date of repudiation i.e., 29.08.2008 till
realization, along with compensation of Rs. 5,00,000/- for mental agony and
harassment, and litigation costs of Rs. 2,00,000/-.
3. The OP No. 1 Bank has filed its detailed affidavit in reply. At the outset,
the Bank has submitted that the complainant was under a mandatory obligation
to insure the stock, as the loan facility had been granted against hypothecation
of stock as security. It is specifically contended that the Bank never acted as an
agent of the Insurance Company, but since the complainant failed to take
insurance despite such obligation, the Bank was constrained to obtain insurance
only to safeguard its own financial interest concerning the secured loan. It is
further stated that upon receiving information about the fire incident dated
06.12.2007, the Bank promptly informed the Insurance Company in writing on
07.12.2007, requesting necessary action for processing the claim, thereby
asserting that the Bank duly discharged its responsibility and did not neglect any
duty in this regard. The Bank has further explained that the complainant's loan
account had subsequently turned into a Non-Performing Asset (NPA) and was
Page 3 of 29
transferred to the Asset Recovery Branch (ARB), Khanpur, Ahmedabad, along
with all records. Recovery proceedings were initiated before the Debt Recovery
Tribunal (DRT) which got settled in 2013 after recovery of Rs.13 lakhs, and the
complainant ultimately settled the account with the ARB. In this background, the
Bank has questioned the conduct of the complainant in pursuing multiple
proceedings without application of mind. It is also contended that the
complainant, after a long delay, approached the Insurance Company vide letter
dated 30.08.2013 seeking reopening of the claim, to which the Insurance
Company replied on 03.09.2013, clearly stating that the complainant had failed
to respond to earlier communications issued by the surveyor (letter dated
28.06.2008) calling for documents and details. The Insurance Company further
stated in its letter dated 29.08.2008 that the complainant had failed to provide
required proof and had submitted fraudulent and altered bills, and had also failed
to produce documentary evidence showing actual payment transactions.
Consequently, the claim was rejected in accordance with policy conditions.
Copies of relevant letters dated 07.12.2007 and 29.08.2008 have been annexed
as Annexure R-1 and R-2 respectively. The Bank has strongly emphasized that
the cause of action arose on 29.08.2008, i.e., the date of repudiation of the
insurance claim, and therefore, the limitation period under
Section 24A
of the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986 commenced from that date. On this point, the
Bank has relied upon the Hon'ble Supreme Court (stated to be reported in 2009
Law Suit (SC) 1310 and 2009 Law Suit (SC) 428), wherein, as submitted, it has
been held that in insurance matters, the cause of action arises either from the
date of incident or of repudiation, and complaints filed beyond the statutory
period of limitation are liable to be dismissed as time-barred unless sufficient
cause is shown. It was contended that the present complaint is clearly barred by
limitation and deserves dismissal on this ground alone. Further, the Bank has
submitted that it had, vide letter dated 19.10.2013, clarified that no stock
statements were available on record, as the complainant had not submitted the
same at the relevant time, and therefore, the Bank cannot be compelled to issue
any certificate or document to support reopening of the claim. It is asserted that
the rejection of the claim was due to the complainant's own wrongful acts,
including submission of false documents, and now the complainant is attempting
to shift the entire blame onto the Bank through unwarranted correspondence and
Page 4 of 29
litigation, causing unnecessary harassment to the Bank. The Bank has further
contended that the complaint suffers from negligence, lack of diligence, and
absence of legal merit, and no sufficient cause has been shown either for
condonation of delay or for grant of any relief. The Bank has prayed that the
complaint and/or delay condonation application be dismissed with costs, being
devoid of merit and barred by limitation.
3.1 The Opponent No.2, The New India Assurance Company Ltd., filed its
written statement/reply before the State Commission denying the allegations
made by the complainant and contending that the complaint was false,
misconceived, not maintainable in law, and liable to be dismissed with costs. The
Insurance Company specifically denied all allegations except those expressly
admitted and submitted that there was no deficiency in service on its part, as the
claim had been repudiated only after proper investigation, verification of
documents, and due application of mind. At the outset, the Insurance Company
raised a preliminary objection regarding the maintainability of the complaint by
contending that the complainant does not fall within the definition of "consumer"
under the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
, since the complainant was allegedly
running a commercial business of jewellery and had not produced any evidence
to show that such activity was for earning livelihood by self-employment. Hence,
according to the Insurance Company, the complaint itself was not maintainable
before the Consumer Forum. The Insurance Company admitted that the
complainant had obtained Shopkeepers Insurance Policy No.
212400/48/07/3400001276 for the period from 22.06.2007 to 21.06.2008, but
denied several factual assertions made in the complaint, including the allegation
that all details and documents had been properly furnished by the complainant. It
was specifically denied that the claim form was filled up by Opponent No.1 Bank
or that the complainant had provided all required stock details and purchase
documents at the relevant time. The Insurance Company further submitted that
after receiving intimation of the fire incident, it appointed Surveyor Mr. S.P. Bhatt
for investigation and assessment of the claim. During the course of investigation,
the surveyor repeatedly demanded necessary documents from the complainant
through letters dated 23.02.2008, 31.03.2008, 28.06.2008, 14.07.2008, and
15.07.2008, seeking supporting documents, stock records, and proof of
purchases for processing the claim. According to the Insurance Company,
Page 5 of 29
although the complainant subsequently submitted certain documents such as
balance sheets, profit and loss accounts, bank stock statements, and purchase
bills, upon verification of the original supplier records and bill books, serious
discrepancies were discovered. It was specifically contended that the surveyor,
while verifying the purchase bills from the suppliers, found that the complainant
had submitted fraudulently altered and inflated bills in support of the insurance
claim. The Insurance Company relied heavily upon the findings of the surveyor
as well as the audit conducted by M/s Pravin F. Shah & Co., Chartered
Accountants, who independently verified the accounts and found that the
complainant had intentionally increased the purchase values in the invoices
compared to the original supplier records. The reply specifically mentions that
bills shown as purchases from M/s Bittu Bindiya Selection ranged from
Rs.50,000/- to Rs.3,11,410/- without proper details regarding quantity, type, or
size of goods, and that such high-value cash transactions were commercially
improbable, thereby creating serious doubt regarding genuineness of the
purchases. The Insurance Company further submitted that after receipt of the
survey report dated 27.08.2008, and after due verification of all records and
documents, it issued the repudiation letter dated 29.08.2008 repudiating the
claim under Policy Conditions No. 6B and 8. It was specifically stated in the reply
that the complainant had failed to furnish complete proof and supporting
information as required by the surveyor and had also submitted fraudulent and
altered bills relating to alleged purchases. Therefore, according to the Insurance
Company, the complainant had violated the terms and conditions of the policy
and consequently forfeited all rights under the insurance contract. The Insurance
Company also denied the complainant's allegation that the repudiation letter was
supplied belatedly on 04.01.2010 and asserted that the repudiation had already
been communicated in 2008 itself. It was further submitted that in the
complainant's own letter dated 30.08.2013, the complainant had admitted that he
was not in a position to submit all documents demanded by the surveyor at the
relevant time, which itself established breach of policy conditions. The Insurance
Company replied to the said letter vide communication dated 03.09.2013,
reiterating that the claim already stood closed and repudiated. Further, the
Insurance Company denied having any personal knowledge regarding the
proceedings before the Debt Recovery Tribunal or other disputes between the
Page 6 of 29
complainant and the Bank. It was also specifically denied that any legal notice
had been served upon the Insurance Company prior to filing of the complaint.
The Insurance Company strongly contended that the repudiation of the claim
was legal, justified, and in accordance with the policy conditions, and therefore
no deficiency in service or unfair trade practice could be attributed to it. It was
further alleged that the complainant had not approached the Commission with
clean hands and had suppressed material facts while filing the complaint. The
Insurance Company also argued that the matter involved complicated questions
of fact requiring oral and documentary evidence, including summoning of
witnesses, and therefore the dispute was essentially civil in nature and not
appropriate for summary adjudication under the
Consumer Protection Act
. The
Insurance Company denied the complainant's entitlement to: (i) Rs.37,16,627/-
with interest @ 12% p.a.; (ii) Rs.5,00,000/- towards mental agony and
harassment; and Rs.2,00,000/- towards litigation costs. It was prayed that the
complaint be dismissed with exemplary costs.
4. At the first instance, in Complaint Case No.177 of 2014, the State
Commission vide its order dated 12.02.2018 allowed the complaint, holding the
Insurance Company liable for deficiency in service. The order is reproduced
herein below:
"11. It would not be out of place to mention here that the bank also did not
 cooperate with the complainant in settlement of his legitimate claim with the
 insurance company though the policy was genuine. On the contrary, the bank has
 filed case before Debts Recovery Tribunal, Ahmedabad against the complainant
 and the complainant settled the case and also obtained No Due Certificate. It is
 also pertinent to note that when hypothecation loan is advanced against stock to
 the customer/borrower then it is incumbent upon the bank to carry out periodical
 inspection of the stock and the premises where the stock is stored and also to
 procure stock statement from the loanee. Nothing is submitted before us to show
 that such an exercise has been carried out by the bank in the present case. The
 complainant quite often requested the opponent insurance company and bank to
 settle the claim but for a long time no reply has been given by either of the parties
 and subsequently the claim was repudiated by the insurance company.
12. We have gone through the terms and conditions of the policy. As per the terms
 and conditions, if any fraudulent claim is submitted, then the same is liable for
 repudiation. But, as discussed above, only allegation of fraud is made but no iota
 of evidence is placed on record to substantiate the said allegation. By merely
 making allegation of fraud, it cannot be said that fraud has been perpetrated.
13. We may also make mention about the allegation made by the complainant
 about illegal gratification from the side of the surveyor as well as the auditor.
 Neither the bank nor the insurance company has refuted this allegation or dealt
 with the same However, we do not propose to enter into the allegation though
 either of the opponents has denied such allegation.
Page 7 of 29
14. Now, let us come to the admissible amount of claim. We have gone through
 the statement of the complainant dated 6.12.2007 recorded by the police in which
 the complainant has set out the details of the damage caused to various stocks,
 furniture, fixture etc. incident took place at midnight of 6.12.2008 and intimation
 was given immediately and without any delay the complainant has given the
 details of damage caused to his stock, complainant is dealing in fancy items,
 personal accessories, imitation jewellery, cosmetics etc. Upon intimation, the
 police reached the site and drew panchnama wherein the estimated loss is stated
 to be in the vicinity of 22,00,000/-. In our opinion, there is no reason to discard this
 evidence, particularly when neither of the opponents has disputed the version of
 the claimant. What the opponents have stated is that the bills produced by the
 complainant are excessive and not tallying with the books of the suppliers of the
 goods.
15. Considering the statement of the complainant before police, in our opinion, the
 complainant must have suffered damages to the stock in the sum of 22,00,000/-.
 The surveyor has assessed the loss caused to furniture and fixtures in the sum of
 194,958/-. Therefore, would come to the total loss suffered by the complainant
 23,00,000/- (rounded up).
16. In view of the above discussion, we pass following order.
ORDER
4 Complaint No. 177 of 2014 is partly allowed. Opponent No.2 The New India
 Assurance Company Limited 1s directed to pay to the complainant
 23,00,000/- Rupees Twenty three lakhs only) with interest @ 9% p.a. from the
 date of complaint till realization and 25,000/- towards cost and compensation
 or mental agony and hardship caused to the complainant. Rest of the claims of
 the complainant is disallowed."
5. Insurance Company aggrieved by the aforesaid order dated 12.02.2018,
 filed First Appeal No. 555 of 2018 before this Commission. This Commission,
 after hearing the parties, disposed of the said appeal vide order dated

 14.08.2019 on the basis of consent of both sides, whereby the impugned order
 was set aside and the matter was remanded back to the State Commission for
 fresh adjudication, with specific directions to permit the parties to lead further
 evidence, including examination and cross-examination of witnesses in respect
 of the disputed invoices. The order is reproduced herein below:
"Dated: 14 Aug 2019
 ORDER
 After hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the appeal is disposed of in
 terms of the following consent order, the consent having been given by the
 learned counsel for the appellant as well as by the learned counsel for the
 complainant on instructions from the complainant namely Mr. Kapur Chand
 who is present in the Court:
1. The impugned order is set aside.
2. The complainant shall either file the affidavits of the persons whose
 invoices he had submitted to the surveyor or shall produce them as
 witness before the State Commission. The appellant company shall
 be entitled to cross-examine such witnesses.
3. The appellant shall be entitled to lead evidence in rebuttal if it so
 desires.
Page 8 of 29
4. The State Commission shall decide the complaint afresh after
 considering the evidence produced in terms of this order as well as
 the evidence including the documents already produced before it.
5. The State Commission shall decide the complaint afresh within four
 months of the parties appearing before it in terms of this order.
6. The amount, which the appellant had deposited in compliance of the
 interim order of this Commission, shall remain deposited till the
 complaint is decided afresh by the State Commission, while deciding
 the complaint.
7. An appropriate order with regard to disbursal of the said amount and
 interest which accrues on it, shall be passed by the State
 Commission.
The parties shall appear before the concerned State Commission on
 17.09.2019."
6. Pursuant to the remand order passed by this Commission on 14.08.2019,
the matter was reconsidered by the State Commission afresh. However, after
re-evaluation of the material on record and the evidence led by the parties, the
State Commission, vide its order dated 12.11.2021, dismissed the complaint.
The State Commission, as per order dated 12.11.2021, held that the complainant
had failed to substantiate his claim with credible and reliable evidence, and that
the material on record, including the surveyor's report, Chartered Accountant's
findings, and the FSL report, clearly established that the complainant had
submitted fraudulent and manipulated purchase bills, thereby violating the policy
conditions. Consequently, in view of the fraud clause under the policy, the entire
claim stood forfeited, and the repudiation of the claim by the Insurance Company
was justified, no deficiency in service could be attributed to either the Insurance
Company or the Bank, and accordingly, the complaint was dismissed without any
relief. The complainant has now filed this present First Appeal before this
Commission on 12.04.2022, assailing the impugned order dated 12.11.2021 and
seeking appropriate reliefs in accordance with law. The order of State
Commission is reproduced herein below:

the surveyor and chartered accountant. Therefore, the repudiation deserves to be
held as justified.
17. Ramlal H. Kumavat, proprietor of Bittu Bindiya Selection, has been
cross-examined (Exh.47, Page No.368). His evidence is to the effect that he is
brother of the complainant, is doing business separately in shop at different location,
Kapurchand gave him lots of Rupees by cash and also by cheques, he does not
remember exactly whether he filed IT Return oftheFY 2006-07 and would produce
it, his statement from Gandhinagar Co-Op. Bank and Union Bank are produced, has
not produced any record to show his having done business with any other than
Kangan Palace, he does not remember whether he had VAT No. or ST No. which he
cannot produced, has not given any receipt of the amounts shown to have been paid
by cash, has not applied any ST in these bills, and it is true that he has not produced
any proof of any amount shown to have been received by cash, clarifies in
re-examination that ST was applicable on certain imitation items and not on others.
Now, no bills of this witness were sent to FSL, and there is no other proof to disprove
the transactions with this witness. But as held that they cannot be held payable as
entire claim is held to be not payable in view of clause 7.

claim by the Insurance Company was primarily on the ground that the
complainant had failed to furnish satisfactory proof of purchase /loss and had
submitted altered and inflated purchase bills, thereby violating the policy
conditions and the principle of utmost good faith. The surveyor, after conducting
investigation and verifying the records from suppliers, categorically reported that
there were material discrepancies and manipulations in the purchase invoices,
which were further corroborated by the Chartered Accountant's audit findings,
indicating that several bills were either inflated or not supported by actual
transactions and that the financial records did not correspond with the claimed
stock position. Further, the FSL report clearly establishes that numerical figures
in various bills were altered in different handwriting by the complainant, thereby

artificially and fraudulently enhancing the value of purchases, which directly
impacts and fraudulently inflates the claimed stock and loss. The complainant,
despite opportunities, failed to produce convincing documentary proof of actual
payments, such as corresponding bank transactions or credible supplier
confirmations, to substantiate the genuineness of the disputed bills. The bank
records and stock statements relied upon by the complainant, though indicative
of certain transactions, do not categorically and sharply point to or conclusively
explain dr establish the authenticity of the inflated figures reflected in the
disputed invoices, particularly in light of the contradictions highlighted by

the applicable policy conditions relating to fraud, once it is established that the
claim is attempted to have been supported by fraudulent or manipulated
documents, the entire claim becomes forfeited. The argument that some portion
of the claim, excluding the alleged inflation, should still be allowed is not tenable
in view of such policy stipulations and the principle of uberrima fide. The role of
the Bank, in the present case, appears limited to financing and facilitating
insurance, and no deficiency in service is made out against it, especially when it
had promptly informed the Insurance Company about the incident. Accordingly,
on a holistic appreciation of the evidence, it is to be noted that the repudiation of
the claim cannot be said to be arbitrary or unjustified, as the same is based on
cogent material, expert reports, and independent verification, which collectively
indicate that the claim was not supported by reliable and genuine documents
and that there is fraudulent attempt to inflate the claim. Therefore, the findings
regarding submission of altered and inflated bills stand substantiated, and the
claim of the complainant does not merit acceptance.

with many of them". The FSL report also clearly establishes such intended
addition of amounts in the bills so as to artificially inflate the purchase. The FSL
report scientifically support such finding firstly of the surveyor and the insurer and
of thereafter of the State Commission. Additionally, the complainant himself in
the complaint in para 6 of the complaint (page 178) has stated that M/s Bittoo
Bindia Selection (from whom also major purchases are stated to have been
made to justify the quantity and value of loss) has been paid cash against
purchases to the extent of as high as Rs.29 lakhs, the fact and source of which
could not be reasonably explained through cogent corroborative material,
though, even if prima facie established, the stale and non-comtemporaneous
evidence or explanation after 5 years of the survey report would have limited
reliability. Though it is the averment in the complaint that "all documents were
submitted", the fundamental issue of dishonest and fraudulent inflation of the
purchases has remained wholly unexplained in the complaint or thereafter. Page
no. 146 to 160 are the copies of the bank statement of M/s Bittoo Bindia
selection (page 146, 147) and of the complainant (page 148 to 160). Page 161
gives the details of alleged payment through bank transfer totalling to Rs.19.17
lakhs made to M/s Bittoo Bindia selection on the strength of which it was averred
before the State Commission that notwithstanding the overwriting in the bills, the
same are genuine. Not only the State Commission has dealt with the issue and
brought out the fallacy of the contention, it has also been demonstrated in para
14 and 15 of the State Commission that the bills presented to the surveyor are
inflated and depict transactions which are far from real and substantially inflated.

correlated so as to establish that alleged payment of Rs. 19.17 lakhs made to M/s

as to from which particular account the amount is debited. In any case, the
amount is not shown to have been debited in the complainant's account on
17.08.2007 because the copy of the complainant's bank statement for the period
August 2007 has not been placed on record. Further, as noted earlier, as per the
complainant's own averment in the complaint, huge cash payment of Rs.29 lakhs
is made to M/s Bindiya and there is no evidence on record regarding the source
of cash and how such cash payment for purchases is made and reflected in the
sales book and the cash book. Similarly, qua the alleged copies of stock
statements allegedly submitted to he Bank, placed at Page No.73 to 109, firstly
these stocks statement do not show any acknowledgement receipt of the Bank.
Secondly, the Bank in its Written version in para 12 has categorically stated that
the complainant has not deposited any stock statement and further that the bank
does not have any such copy on record. Otherwise also the mere filing of stock
statement with the bank showing any arbitrary figure therein does not in itself
establish the quantum and value of stock as on the date of the incident. Thus,
the Bank statements or stock-statements allegedly submitted to the Bank or any
other records, in our opinion also, do not refute or dilute the serious and
conclusive evidence of fraud and dishonesty in manipulating the documents
(purchase bills) submitted to the surveyor in support of the claim and therefore

13. Be that as it may, the dishonest and fraudulent manipulation of the
purchase bills with inflation component of Rs.6.19 lakhs is unimpeachably
established on record. Therefore, we have no hesitation in holding that the
insurer and the State Commission are absolutely right in their conclusion that
the complainant has violated the fundamental condition of uberrima fide
incorporated in condition no.7/8 of the policy as reproduced by State
Commission in para 8, as rightly concluded by the State Commission in that
para. The evidenced dishonestly and fraud on the part of the complainant for
enhancing the claim goes to the root of the insurance contract and the insurer is
absolutely justified in wholly repudiating the liability. We also find no substance in
the contention on behalf of the complainant that the State Commission exceeded
its jurisdiction by overstepping the limited directions of this Commission while
remanding the matter. As such, the reference to FSL has assisted the State
Commission in re-considering and re-appreciating the evidence brought on
record and indeed the State Forum has inherent powers to make expert
reference as and when considered necessary even during remand proceedings
when there is neither any express direction nor any express bar in the remand
order of this Commission. Also, the State Commission's order dated 25.02.2020
allowing the insurance company's application for such reference to the
Forensic/handwriting expert appears to have attained finality by not having been
challenged before any higher fora. The reliance placed by the Ld. Counsel for the
complainant on decisions as cited in para 9 supra is also misplaced for two
reasons. First, the decisions are in the context of criminal proceedings while the
proceedings before the State Commission are not only civil in nature but they are
also of summary nature wherein the evidence is to be evaluated not on the basis
of "beyond reasonable doubt", but on the basis of preponderance of probability.
Second, the handwriting expert's report is not the sole basis for the State
Commission to have arrived at its findings. There were already material in the
nature of survey report, which as per the settled principle is a primary and
significant piece of evidence, CA's report and the fact of dishonest insertion of
amounts in the purchase bills evident even to the naked eyes. The State
Commission has also duly and minutely considered the affidavits of the

complainant as also the proprietor of M/s Bitto Bindia and concluded that the
 same is of no assistance to the complainant in establishing his claim. Moreover,
 though not noted by the State Commission, we cannot overlook the fact that the
 proprietor/partners of M/s JalaRam Enterprises, M/s Dhiraj Jewellers, M/s
 Shivam Bangles and M/s Skyline, the parties whose bills are found to have been
 manipulated by the complainant, have not been presented for any
 cross-examination. On the other hand, the affidavits of the surveyor Shri Sunil
. Kumar P. Bhatt as also of the Chartered accountant Shri Pravin Kumar Shah
 have been filed by the insurance company wherein both of them have reiterated
 the findings given by them. These have duly been considered by the State
 Commission in para 13 of the order. After considering the totality of the facts, we
 are therefore of the considered opinion that the claim of the complainant was
 based on altered, inflated and unreliable documents, and the repudiation by the
 Insurance Company was fully justified and was in accordance with policy
 conditions and with the violation of the solemn principle of utmost good faith. If
 the insured engages into dishonest means for enhancing or supporting the
 indemnification amount, the insurer would be fully entitled to repudiate the whole
 claim. Accordingly, the findings recorded by the State Commission do not suffer
 from any error of fact or law warranting any interference. The present Appeal
 therefore lacks merit and is accordingly dismissed and the impugned order dated
 12.11.2021 is affirmed. No order as to costs.
